html:
The Walmajarri are an Aboriginal Australian people of the northern edge of the Great Sandy Desert in Western Australia, south of the Fitzroy valley. The map shows them as Walmatjarri from 1600 to 1815.

They were desert people, moving between wells and soaks across the sandhill country. Their neighbours were the Gooniyandi and Bunuba to the north, the Mangala to the west and the Kukatja to the southeast. During the 20th century most Walmajarri families walked north out of the desert to the cattle stations of the Fitzroy River, and many now live in and around Fitzroy Crossing. Their language is still spoken.
